icons.instructions: Use specific lucid-react icons: Check for completed steps, LayoutDashboard for dashboard, Calculator for estimate, Activity for process, Settings for admin, Bell for notifications, User for avatar, TrendingUp/Down for trends.

accessibility_and_interactions.hover_states: All buttons and table rows must have visual hover feedback.
accessibility_and_interactions.transparent_backgrounds: CRITICAL: Do not use fully transparent backgrounds for dropdowns, popovers, or floating menus. Always use bg-white with shadow-lg and border.
accessibility_and_interactions.testing: All interactive elements MUST include a data-testid attribute (e.g., data-testid='save-estimate-button', data-testid='base-unit-select').

instructions_to_main_agent: You are building a high-fidelity replica of an enterprise Construction Cost Estimator based on the provided problem statement specifications.
Construct a full-page flex layout. Left sidebar (navy blue #0B1120), center canvas (slate-50 bg, scrollable), and a slim right toolbar for quick actions.
Implement the Header with Base Unit and Currency dropdowns, Recalculate and Save buttons.
Build the 6-step horizontal progress stepper exactly as requested.
Create a grid of 6 KPI metric cards. Use the specific background and text colors detailed in colors.kpi_metrics for their icons.
Build a robust Tab navigation bar (Summary, Cost Breakdown, BOQ, Utilities, etc.). Implement dummy state to toggle active tab visually.
In the main content, place a Recharts Donut chart (Cost Breakdown) alongside a Line chart (Cost Trend).
Build the 'Top 12 Cost Items' data table with columns: #, Activity, Quantity, Unit, Rate, Amount, % of Total.
Add 'Key Assumptions' list with green checks, and 'Risk & Cost Drivers' with yellow warning icons.
At the bottom, place the 7 utility demand metric cards (Water, Steam, Chiller, Power, etc.) with colorful icons.
In the bottom of the left sidebar, add an 'Active Project' info box showing FX Rate and unit settings.
Use Shadcn UI for standard elements (Buttons, Dropdowns) but customize them heavily using Tailwind to achieve the required dense enterprise look.
Do NOT add global transitions like 'transition: all' in CSS. Manage transitions via Tailwind classes.
Create all elements in React (.js files, not .tsx).
UNIVERSAL GUIDELINES FOR MAIN AGENT: You tend to converge toward generic, 'on distribution' outputs. In frontend design, this creates what users call the 'AI slop' aesthetic. Avoid this: make creative, distinctive frontends that surprise and delight.
Dark colors look good when used independently without gradients. DO NOT use dark colors as gradients.
Don't make generic centered layouts, simplistic gradients, and uniform styling.
Create depth through layered design elements with z-index hierarchy.
Use glass-morphism effects with backdrop filters (12-24px blur) where appropriate, BUT DO NOT use transparent backgrounds for overlays with content underneath.
You MUST NOT apply universal transition. Eg: transition: all. This results in breaking transforms. Always add transitions for specific interactive elements like button, input excluding transforms.
You MUST NOT center align the app container, ie do not add .App { text-align: center; } in the css file. This disrupts the human natural reading flow of text.
Always use modern button styles like pill-shaped, or sharp button with interaction animations & color relevant to the app style.
NEVER: use AI assistant Emoji characters like 🤖🧠💭💡🔮🎯 etc for icons. Use lucide-react.
Every interaction needs micro-animations - hover states, transitions, parallax effects, and entrance animations. Static = dead.
Use 2-3x more spacing than feels comfortable. Cramped designs look cheap.
Subtle grain textures, noise overlays, custom cursors, selection states, and loading animations: separates good from extraordinary.
Prioritize using pre-existing components from src/components/ui when applicable.
Use sonner for toasts, located in /app/src/components/ui/sonner.tsx.
